observations: A truck-mounted borehole drilling rig (drilling mast/boom and frame) mounted on a white cab-over truck.
Photos show heavy rust/dust on the rig frame and components; no clear view of brand/model plates for the drilling rig.
Photo 0 shows the front of the truck and the rig structure; the truck front grille/branding is partially visible but not clearly readable.
Photo 1 shows the side of the truck and rig; hydraulic hoses/cables are visible but condition (leaks/tears) can’t be confirmed from photos.
Photo 2 shows the rear/front area with the rig mast/boom; again, no clearly readable model/serial numbers for the rig or engine.

claims.claim: Very sound and working fine borehole drilling machine
claims.evidence: No photo shows the machine operating (drilling in progress), gauges, or a working test.
Photos only show the machine parked; no evidence of site readiness (spares, tools, transport condition, or recent job output).
This is marketing language; photos do not verify buyer seriousness or any technical condition.

risks.risk: Whether the drilling system actually works (engine power, mast movement, drilling rotation, hydraulics) — photos can’t confirm operation.
risks.proof: A short video of the rig drilling (spindle/rotary action + mast movement) with sound and visible RPM/flow if available.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst case: needs repair/overhaul).

risks.risk: Hydraulic leaks or worn hoses/cylinders (common on rig attachments) — not reliably visible in still photos.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all hydraulic hoses/couplings + a video running hydraulics through full extension/retraction with no seepage.
risks.if_unproven: Price as possible hydraulic issues (worst case: hoses/cylinders may need replacement).

risks.risk: Missing/incorrect drilling consumables (bit, rods, casing, mud pump parts) — photos don’t show the full drilling kit.
risks.proof: Inventory list with photos of the complete drilling set (bit, rods, casing if any, pump/hoses, control panel parts).
risks.if_unproven: Price as incomplete kit (worst case: buyer must source missing parts).

risks.risk: Truck condition (engine, gearbox, brakes, tyres) — only exterior condition is visible.
risks.proof: Start-up video (cold start if possible) + undercarriage/brake check + tyre tread close-ups.
risks.if_unproven: Price as truck may need servicing (worst case: mechanical work required).

risks.risk: Rig capacity/specs (depth, diameter range, model of drilling head) — cannot be read from photos.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the rig/spec plate or manual label showing capacity and drilling head model.
risks.if_unproven: Price at lowest/unknown capacity assumption (worst case: limited performance).

proof_requests: Video of the rig operating: drilling in progress (rotation + mast movement) for at least a few minutes.
Close-up photos of hydraulic hoses/cylinders and couplings, plus a running hydraulics test video.
Photos and list of the full drilling consumables/kit included (bit, rods, casing/pump parts if applicable).
Clear photos of any identification plates: truck VIN/engine plate and rig/spec plate (capacity, drilling head model).
Truck start-up and driving/engagement video (or at least start + idle + brake/gear test).
response.reason: The photos confirm a truck-mounted borehole drilling rig, but they do not prove it is working or provide readable specs/identifiers needed to price it confidently. The seller’s “working fine” claim is unverified remotely, so the correct next step is operational and spec proof.
